enforcement.tokenBoundary: Checked before run_code and nested calls; an in-flight provider response cannot be interrupted at an exact token, and this budget never aborts the outer Agent.
enforcement.tokenMetric: Runtime charges only newly generated assistant Usage.output tokens, including reasoning. recommended.maxTotalTokens is retained as the legacy benchmark config key; input and cached context do not consume the per-task budget.

common.note: Task call/token budgets and independent per-run compute/wall ceilings are enforced by model ID. Model thinking and ordinary tools do not consume run time. maxEstimatedSubCalls describes expected work; maxTotalSubCalls is the hard limit with correction headroom. Workload-size fields remain advisory because the extension cannot infer record/shard counts from arbitrary code.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol.rationale: C4 was clean 3/3 and C6 was correct 2/2 with roughly 41k tokens. Most stable PTC model in this benchmark.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra.rationale: C4 was clean 3/3 and C6 was clean 2/2. Occasional path retry was observed below the boundary.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna.rationale: C6 was clean 2/2 after the stdin race fix. Lower levels showed more self-correction and path retries than Sol/Terra.

dashscope/deepseek-v4-flash.rationale: C4 was semantically correct 3/3 historically. Monitored policy runs needed provider/final-formatting time, one extra merge program, and up to nine discovery/re-read calls beyond the 31-call estimate; the 40-call hard cap covers that bounded correction headroom. C5/C6 remained correct but consumed about 1.10M/1.49M tokens, so multi-program complexity is not economical.

dashscope/deepseek-v4-pro.rationale: C4 is the conservative unattended limit. The 120-second per-run wall ceiling accommodates slow nested-tool waits without charging provider or final-formatting time; C5 passed but was slow and expensive, while C6 failed 0/2.
